steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: stdio works locally and nowhere else. Streamable HTTP (2025-03-26) is the remote standard. The old HTTP+SSE transport is deprecated and being removed in mid-2026. Picking the wrong transport costs a migration; picking the right one buys a remote-hostable MCP server with session continuity and DNS-rebinding protection.

steps.title: The problem
cards: The first MCP remote transport (2024-11) was HTTP+SSE: two endpoints, one for the client's POSTs and one Server-Sent-Events channel for the server-to-client stream. It worked. It was also clumsy: two endpoints per session, broken caches in front of some CDNs, and a hard dependency on long-lived SSE connections that some WAFs terminate aggressively.

The 2025-03-26 spec replaced it with Streamable HTTP: one endpoint, POST for client requests, GET for establishing a session stream, both sharing a `Mcp-Session-Id` header. Every server built or migrated since then uses Streamable HTTP. The old SSE mode is being deprecated — Atlassian Rovo removed it June 30, 2026; Keboola April 1, 2026; most remaining enterprise servers by end of 2026.

And stdio still matters for local servers. Claude Desktop, VS Code, and every IDE-shaped client spawn servers via stdio. The right mental model: stdio for "this machine", Streamable HTTP for "over the network". No cross-over.
